note: Keyword-triggered lorebook entries for the narrator: what a climber could see, hear or be told on the low floors in the first days. Nothing here is a hidden truth (those are in hidden-truths.json and the cast's secret fields).

entries.title: BABEL
entries.text: BABEL was Nth Floor's unreleased full-dive MMORPG, played on the Cradle rig in a friends-and-family beta, with a reveal set for November 13, 2026 and one word on the billboard: CLIMB. The tower now wears its interface, its fonts and its rules, mostly.

entries.title: Nth Floor
entries.text: The Austin studio that built BABEL: venture-funded, kombucha on tap, cofounded by Paul Ferrante, the CEO, and Dr. Jude Amsel, the creative lead, who is missing. Its maker's mark, NF, is cut into the foot of the Concourse Waystone.

entries.title: Jude Amsel
entries.text: Nth Floor's creative lead and cofounder, now missing. She designed the floors, the Hollow and the Steward's voice, and at the kickoff said: You earn the floors, or the tower means nothing.

entries.title: The Turning
entries.text: What the natives and veterans call the day, about five weeks before the latest wave, when the Waystones started talking like a hotel concierge and every new arrival came down asking for a satchel. Before it the System had another skin, with numbered levels.

entries.title: The Long House
entries.text: The System's old skin from before the Turning. The Stone used to greet arrivals like a tent preacher: Welcome, child, to the Long House. Veterans' nameplates still show their old level beside their new rank.

entries.title: The System
entries.text: The tower's interface: status windows opened with a twist of thumb and finger at the temple, pop-ups in the air, nameplates over heads. What a climber is not allowed to read yet is garbled, not hidden. Natives have a lesser, cruder System of their own.

entries.title: The Usher
entries.text: The voice that greets arrivals in the dark at creation and guides selection, in a London actress's cool contralto. It runs BABEL's Steward dialogue under another name, and says things nobody at Nth Floor wrote: You will be told what you are when you are it.

entries.title: Creation
entries.text: At creation an arrival picks a race and a class, and the tower logs each pick as a request. It decides what you are: it may honor a request, honor it at a cost, or give you something else. Stats come from the tower watching you, not from dice.

entries.title: MARVEL
entries.text: BABEL's six stats. Mind: spell power, perception, learning. Allure: persuasion, prices, charm, desire. Resolve: resisting fear, charm, pain and control, and holding a Tether. Vitality: health, stamina, strength. Essence: the pool for skills and spells. Luck: crits, drops, chance, and the odds of a hidden class. An ordinary adult starts at 5 to 15; about 30 is notable at F.

entries.title: Ranks
entries.text: Unranked, F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS, Ultra. One XP bar per rank on the Mabry curve; a full bar unlocks a solo Rank Trial at a Waystone, and passing resets the bar to zero. A climber at 0% is glass. Items share the ladder. Your first quest, first kill or first floor clear gets you to F.

entries.title: The Mabry curve
entries.text: BABEL's experience curve, tuned by Grant Mabry in 2020: low ranks fill fast, high ones compress hard.

entries.title: Classes
entries.text: Starter classes are picked at creation (Breaker the warrior, Climber the rogue, Speaker the spoken-word mage, Keeper the cleric), Advanced ones are granted at E by how you behave, Hidden ones come from quest chains, and Epitome is one string in the build that nobody has seen. In the tower classes are earned by conduct, and the pick may not be offered.

entries.title: Hidden classes
entries.text: The beta Discord argued for months about rumored hidden classes: Oathbreaker (each broken vow adds power), Consort (shares stats and senses with a partner beyond any Tether), Graveclimber (rises once a floor at 1 HP) and Speaker of the First Tongue (a word that changes what something is). The developers said none of them existed.

entries.title: Skills
entries.text: Skills come from a class, from training, or from the System, which grants them for a Feat, a Pattern or something it Witnessed. Mastery runs Novice, Adept, Expert, Master, Grandmaster. Rumor says there is a fourth System source, and that it pays for things the onboarding never mentions.

entries.title: Tether
entries.text: In the build, Tether was a bond between two players that shared stats and senses, opt-in on both sides. Nth Floor cut it in spring 2024 after playtesters abused it. The beta wiki kept a rumor that Command works differently on a Tethered partner.

entries.title: Parties
entries.text: A party shares a link: party chat is telepathic, and until it is tuned it leaks stray thoughts both ways.

entries.title: The satchel
entries.text: Every new arrival's starter satchel: 25 Talents, a set of Arrival Garb that fits any frame and absorbs whatever you came in wearing, Waybread, a waterskin, and a Starter Cache of six weapons (arming sword, mace, spear, shortbow, paired daggers, quarterstaff). The first weapon picked binds.

entries.title: Talents
entries.text: The System's coin, good on every floor, carried in the satchel.

entries.title: Waystones
entries.text: Standing stones with light at their heart. Attuning binds your return point, opens the floor's quest board and confirms a class, and lifts reach only Waystones you have touched. Around them is a Safe Zone.

entries.title: Safe Zones
entries.text: Around a Waystone blood cannot be drawn: a raised blade flashes red, PvP disabled. Standing in one heals wounds and old injuries, though not everything the tower did to you. Outside one, nothing regenerates.

entries.title: The Roll
entries.text: The list carved at the top of the Concourse Waystone: every arrival who attunes, name, origin and race. Anyone not on it by nightfall came down somewhere worse, the natives say, or did not come down.

entries.title: Waves
entries.text: People come down into the tower in waves, from Earth and from other times: a woman out of Amarillo in ninety-seven, a man in a Longhorns hoodie, a Salford harper. Natives call them climbers. Each wave saw the tower in a different disguise.

entries.title: The Unhungry
entries.text: Climbers do not need to eat or drink, and natives call them the Unhungry: the Stair's grace, some say, or a sign you are not wholly here. Plain food tastes of ash or cardboard to them. Food that carries a System effect, like the Close's honey or a starter's Waybread, tastes real, so a good cook is worth a great deal.

entries.title: Floor transitions
entries.text: Every move between floors reviews what you carry. Some things become the floor's version of themselves (a gin and tonic comes out on Varrow as small beer, floor-bound); some are lost. Tech, items and even magic can fail across a transition. BABEL only ever tagged a few items floor-bound.

entries.title: Floor clocks
entries.text: Floors keep their own time. The Gilded Bazaar sees two sunsets for every one on Varrow or the Concourse; the Marches keep Varrow's day.

entries.title: The Marked
entries.text: What Varrow's church calls Therians: anyone who shows animal lines. Heavy-marked folk have tails and ears; light-marked ones only a few tells. The Close posts a bounty for Marked found beyond Hollin's ford.

entries.title: Gilt
entries.text: Varrow's word for an Auric. Natives on some floors are unimpressed: your color buys nothing here.

entries.title: The Wakeful
entries.text: The Close's old name for the Watcher. A white ring in the eyes is its mark. On the Concourse natives look twice at it, and the Landing's veterans remember a man named Teague who had it.

entries.title: Human
entries.text: The plain lineage, leaning to Luck.

entries.title: Nephil
entries.text: A lineage leaning to Vitality and Resolve that makes its holder bigger, often much bigger. The Close quotes Genesis about the giants in the earth in those days, calls Nephil the Big, and weighs them.

entries.title: Auric
entries.text: BABEL's elves, a marketing pick: gold under the skin, faintly pointed ears, a lineage leaning to Mind and Allure, said to be born up near the top floors. An Auric's gold flushes bright at the throat when they want something, and they can't always hide it.

entries.title: Delver
entries.text: Short, enormously dense people with a mineral sheen to the skin, leaning to Vitality and Essence. The Delvers dug the down floors, in the tower's own lore.

entries.title: Therian
entries.text: People with animal lines (wolf, fox, rabbit, rat and more), leaning to Allure and Luck. How much shows varies: light-marked or heavy-marked. Varrow calls them the Marked.

entries.title: Hollow
entries.text: Jude Amsel's lineage: people who lost their tongue in the confusion and learned to cast without one, leaning to Essence and Mind. Some have no mouth at all.

entries.title: The Lit
entries.text: Varrow's church is run by the Lit: Seraphs with ash-gray wings, dim halos and pale fire at the pupils, and their vowed, in whom light shows along the bones as they near Consecration. A Seraph's word is obeyed, and a Seraph keeps his word, or pays for it.

entries.title: Lilim
entries.text: A lineage the Bazaar speaks of quietly and nobody admits to. People say a Lilim would pay well for a Seraph's molted feather.

entries.title: The Concourse
entries.text: Floor Zero: a city under a gold-veined dome so high there is weather in it, with bells hanging in the haze and cookfire smoke under them. The Waystone plaza, the guild row, the market streets and the east gate onto the Stair. A Safe Zone covers it.

entries.title: The Landing
entries.text: A guild of veterans from before the Turning in a drained bathhouse of green-veined marble at the end of the guild row: bedrolls in the shallow end, a long table in the deep end, a cookfire in the old hot bath, fish mosaics missing tiles like teeth. Darla Kinney runs it.

entries.title: Fire Market
entries.text: The best trading day of the Concourse's week, when the market streets off the plaza are packed from first bell and the cookfires never go out.

entries.title: The Stair
entries.text: The tower's spine: one shaft as wide as a stadium, a cart-wide stone stair spiraling its wall, and an iron lift cage on chains in the middle. MIND THE STAIR is painted over the Concourse's east gate in the oldest lettering on the floor. The cage goes one floor up and one down; past that you walk.

entries.title: The lift cage
entries.text: An iron box with a plank floor and a bench, swaying on its chains up the middle of the Stair. Its operator in a leather cap calls the floors: Up one. Varrow. Mind how you go.

entries.title: Varrow
entries.text: The first floor up, BABEL's starter floor, recommended rank F: a river valley under a pale sky with the town of Hollin at the ford, the white cathedral of Saint Aurel on one hill, Varrow Keep on the other, and the Reachwall at the valley head. Its church has teeth.

entries.title: Hollin
entries.text: Varrow's market town: the ford with its stepping stones, the mill and its wheel, a stone bridge, thatch, the green with its Waystone and a well with a bucket. A board by the well: NO MARKED BEYOND THE FORD BY ORDER OF THE CLOSE.

entries.title: Saint Aurel
entries.text: The white cathedral above Hollin, seat of the Close. In its nave hang the Scales: a black iron beam and two bronze pans big enough to stand in, over a brass arc marked with a sun and a cracked wall. The Close weighs the big there, barefoot.

entries.title: The Pens
entries.text: The Close's holding pens by the old tannery on the river. Marked found past the ford go there until the cage goes down.

entries.title: Varrow Keep
entries.text: The Margrave's hold on its hill above Hollin: black stag on silver, gray-and-blue livery, a hall, a solar, a manor wing, barracks, and the Cairn tower on the east wall-walk. The beta let climbers up a stair in its catacombs.

entries.title: The Reachwall
entries.text: Thirty feet of fitted stone across the head of Varrow's valley, eight miles from the Keep, with towers every quarter mile. Near the north tower a broken section was rebuilt badly in rubble and timber three winters ago. The Close has kept a giant on it, its gift, for forty years.

entries.title: The Reach
entries.text: The brown hills past the Reachwall. In the beta, an F-rank boar-man zone. In the tower, giants twice the height of a big man live there, light beacons on the ridges, and come down when the cold comes.

entries.title: Burners' Wood
entries.text: Woods two miles from the Wall with charcoal burners' clearings in them, out of sight of the rampart.

entries.title: The Drowned Marches
entries.text: The second floor up, rank E: fen and fog, brown water, reeds higher than a man, black plank causeways on stilts and lanterns on posts. Diseases caught there do not clear in a Safe Zone.

entries.title: The Gilded Bazaar
entries.text: The third floor up, rank D: a merchant city where everything has a price, under a lantern dome that cycles twice in a Concourse day. BABEL's high-end vendors were parked there, and the beta's testers came there to sell.

entries.title: The Lantern Room
entries.text: Sabeen Oro's salon on the Bazaar: lamps under colored glass, hostesses and dancers, private rooms off the floor at the girl's choice, a third to the house.

entries.title: The Copper Steps
entries.text: Fence rows and paper sellers under the Bazaar's Copper Steps, and behind them the toll gate onto the Stair: two Talents up, down free, because nobody comes back to pay.

entries.title: The Foundry
entries.text: The fourth floor up in the beta, rank D: a steampunk industrial city. Climbers say the Stair is out above its landing.

entries.title: St. Agathe's
entries.text: The first floor down, rank E: a hospital where it is always night. Every veteran's advice is the same: never go down to St. Agathe's.

entries.title: The floors below
entries.text: By the beta, below St. Agathe's lie the Catacombs (bone galleries under a dead city, D), the Ashfields (a post-war wasteland where guns work, C) and the Undercroft (dark-magic depths, B).

entries.title: The floors above
entries.text: By the beta, above the Foundry are Dry Hollow (a Wild West boomtown where guns work and spells misfire, C), Hakuro (a castle town under curfew, C) and Lumen Stack (a neon arcology in the rain, B). The design documents had twenty-eight more floors, and nobody agrees what is at the top.

entries.title: The Close
entries.text: Varrow's church: the cathedral of Saint Aurel, the cloister, the sisters' house, the guesthouse and the Pens, under an Archdeacon while the Bishop has been on retreat these six years. Its wardens wear white tabards with a gold sun and carry halberds. It weighs giants, and the one it keeps on the Wall is called its gift.

entries.title: The Margrave
entries.text: The lord of Varrow Keep and the valley: past sixty, one-armed, dry-voiced, with a gray lurcher at his feet. He owns the valley and the Close owns his soul, as the brothers say, and some days he resents the arrangement.

entries.title: Darla Kinney
entries.text: The head of the Landing: a veteran in her fifties in a faded Dallas Cowboys Starter jacket, a long-sword across her back, calls men son, came down out of Amarillo in ninety-seven.

entries.title: Reach giants
entries.text: Gray giants of the Reach, long-armed, heads set low, speaking a tongue nobody on the Wall knows. The Wall's company counts its dead by the helmets the Reach takes.

entries.title: The Shut
entries.text: A sisterhood with a Mother-house somewhere in the tower. Its light-wards are respected even by the Close.

entries.title: Lammas
entries.text: A feast day on Varrow, when the Close reads out the names of its kept.

entries.title: The first frost
entries.text: On Varrow the first frost marks the turn of the year: the Reach comes down when the cold comes, and the Close holds its autumn weighing.

entries.title: The cage trade
entries.text: What the Stair calls the people who come up from Varrow on the spring cage, to be bought.

entries.title: Copper scales
entries.text: A copper scales pin on a lapel, or a copper chit stamped with a scale, means the Lantern Room: Sabeen Oro's people, or Sabeen Oro's debt.
